name: Borexino

facility_roles.note: facility:lngs already exists (owned by the dark-matter/facilities workstreams) and is referenced here, not edited.

intervals.label: construction
intervals.quote: In 1990, the design was fundamentally altered, and the name of the experiment was changed to "Borexino". Research and development began on the detector at that time. ... By 2004, the structure of the detector had been completed
intervals.note: Sourced from Wikipedia (rank 12) only this session.

intervals.label: data taking
intervals.quote: by May 2007 the detector chamber had been filled and data taking began ... The entire Borexino experiment was terminated in October 2021.
intervals.note: Sourced from Wikipedia (rank 12) only; the official site's own homepage this session described '35 years of operation through 2025' without giving exact start/end dates, which is not used here as it appears to describe the collaboration's overall lifetime (proposal to final analysis) rather than the detector's active data-taking window.

intervals.label: shut down
intervals.quote: the entire Borexino experiment was terminated in October 2021
intervals.note: Terminal event date sourced from Wikipedia (rank 12) only.

physics_goals.value: Directly detect and spectroscopically measure low-energy solar neutrinos (pp, 7Be, pep, 8B and CNO) in real time
physics_goals.quote: A solar neutrino detector designed to observe neutrinos produced in the Sun's nuclear fusion processes.

unique_capabilities.value: Unprecedentedly radio-pure, large-volume liquid-scintillator detector able to see the CNO-cycle neutrino signal for the first time
unique_capabilities.quote: the unprecedentedly radio-pure large-volume liquid-scintillator Borexino detector located at the underground Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso in Italy

quantity.quote: The active neutrino target, 278 t of ultrapure liquid scintillator
quantity.note: 278 t is the active liquid-scintillator mass stated in the 2014 Nature pp-neutrino paper (Methods); Wikipedia's infobox gives the same figure. The nominal fiducial mass is recorded separately on detector:borexino (specs.fiducial_mass); the pp analysis itself used a 75.5 t fiducial cut.

quantity.quote: Protected by 3,800 meters of water-equivalent depth
quantity.note: Sourced from Wikipedia (rank 12) only; differs from the ~1400 m rock / average LNGS overburden figure already recorded on site:lngs-hall-c (owned by the facilities workstream) because m.w.e. and rock-metres are different units and per-hall shielding can differ from the site average.

website.note: The certificate-mismatched domain borexino.lngs.infn.it redirects to/matches borex.lngs.infn.it; the latter is recorded as the working URL fetched this session.

summary.plain: A giant ball of ultra-pure liquid deep under the Gran Sasso mountain in Italy that directly watched low-energy neutrinos streaming from the Sun's core, including two kinds no one had ever seen before.
summary.technical: Liquid-scintillator (pseudocumene+PPO) solar-neutrino detector at LNGS Hall C, 278 t active mass (~100 t fiducial), built 1990-2004, took data May 2007-October 2021. First direct spectral measurement of pp-chain neutrinos (2014) and first experimental evidence of CNO-cycle solar neutrinos (2020).
